beats.summary: Michael cannot find his hotel reservation for the Vancouver Olympics despite having booked it for three years.

evidence.snippet: Michael: Hello Vancouver, this is Michael Scott calling from the United States of America! I have a reservation in your fair city from February 12th to the 19th, first week of the Olympics.
Hotel Employee: Uh, sir? A lot of people are trying to get last-minute reservations at hotels here for the Olympics, but we've been fully booked for months.

beats.summary: Jo Bennett, the new CEO of Sabre, visits the office and introduces herself with a colorful personal background.

evidence.snippet: Jo: I'm Jolene Bennett, Jo for short. I'm a breast cancer survivor, close, personal friends with Nancy Pelosi, and Truman Capote and I slept with three of the same guys.

beats.summary: Jo Bennett interacts with the office staff, noting the co-manager situation and making humorous remarks.

evidence.snippet: Jo (gesturing to Michael): I thought this guy was the manager?
Jo: Two guys doing one job? We gotta do something about that!

beats.summary: Andy prepares Valentine's Day cards for the office, including one for Erin, while trying to avoid seeming too eager.

evidence.snippet: Erin (opening card): Oh, you did? Aw, a bird and a dog!

beats.summary: Pam shows Jim that salesmen can make more money than managers according to the new handbook.

evidence.snippet: Pam: So, check this out. According to the handbook, you could make more money as a salesman than as a manager.
Jim: This is way more than I make now.

beats.summary: Jim expresses that he is not going to miss being manager and admits he is motivated by money and women.

evidence.snippet: Jim: I don't think I'm gonna miss being manager.
